A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NarrativeBridge, the CTN caption benchmark, and CEN. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across formatting and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning comparisons, architecture ablations, cross-dataset evaluations, and qualitative experiments on MSVD and MSR-VTT, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds vision-language model comparisons, a human evaluation study, and a CLIP-versus-BLIP encoder experiment.

M1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds an evaluated CEN variant replacing CLIP encoders with BLIP encoders, a limited component substitution. The principal CTN-generation pipeline, two-stage CEN architecture, and losses remain unchanged. Statements that both encoders process the whole video clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain MSVD and MSR-VTT captioning coverage. Cross-dataset tests and the unlabeled-video demonstration already appear in v1. The human study samples existing CTN captions; the new NExT-QA examples illustrate benchmark differences without evaluating the method on that dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds VideoLLaVA and ShareGPT4Video, each evaluated zero-shot, with LoRA fine-tuning, and with full-model fine-tuning. These substantially broaden the comparison beyond the retained SEM-POS, AKGNN, and GIT baselines. Figure 5 also adds outputs from both VLMs.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a human evaluation protocol with five experts rating 100 randomly sampled validation captions, 50 per dataset, on three criteria. It also adds VLM fine-tuning protocols and an alternative-encoder configuration. Existing CEN splits, training budgets, sampling rules, and automatic metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 adds systematic human assessment of causal accuracy, temporal coherence, and relevance. Appendix A.6 newly tests dependence on the visual encoder through CLIP-versus-BLIP results. Existing architecture, transfer, prompting, and automatic-filtering analyses are retained; Figure 5 expands comparative failure examples.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 reports rating standard deviations and absolute-agreement intraclass correlation with a 95% confidence interval for the human study. This introduces substantive variability and reliability reporting. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed-based uncertainty for the captioning-model scores.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 and Table 2 scores are retained, while VLM, BLIP, and human-rating results are added. On MSR-VTT, full-fine-tuned VideoLLaVA and ShareGPT4Video score 19.98 and 20.76 CIDEr versus CEN's unchanged 49.87. BLIP-CEN scores 43.01. New MSVD SPICE results make VideoLLaVA Simple FT, at 16.09, the runner-up ahead of GIT's 15.58.

T1.justification: The similarity definition, feature construction, contrastive objectives, decoding formulation, and losses in Equations 1–9 are unchanged. Neither version presents additional theorems or proofs; the new human-rating statistics do not introduce a mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly extend the superiority claim to fine-tuned VLMs and add a strong cross-dataset generalization claim. The central contributions remain the CTN benchmark and CEN architecture; human evaluation supplies additional support for the retained caption-quality claim.

C2.justification: v2 newly describes the unchanged transfer results as strong generalization, while retaining v1's warning about substantial zero-shot performance drops. It also interprets human ratings as benchmark validation and BLIP results as architectural flexibility. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds VLM implementation details: A100-80GB hardware, LoRA applied to the LLM at learning rate 2e-4, and full-model AdamW fine-tuning with initial rate 1e-3, cosine scheduling, and 0.03 warmup ratio. Original CEN implementation details and the benchmark-release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to VideoLLaVA, ShareGPT4Video, BLIP, and AdamW. It expands positioning against recent VLMs and elaborates the distinction from the already-cited NExT-QA through Appendix A.7. The overall research positioning remains centered on holistic causal-temporal captioning.

P1.justification: Targeted passages in the abstract, introduction, related work, and results are expanded or rewritten. Results gain numbered subsections, and appendices A–F become subsections within Appendix A with new material inserted. Most method descriptions, prompt analyses, and limitations retain their wording.

P2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 5 expand to include VLM comparisons. New Tables 3–5 display human ratings, encoder results, and benchmark distinctions; a new Figure 18 illustrates NExT-QA. Existing later figures are retained and renumbered. Typography, running headers, and placement change, while the principal diagrams and plots remain intact.

improvement.justification: v1 supports CTN caption quality mainly through automatic relevance filtering and selected examples. v2 adds direct expert assessment with reliability statistics, substantially broader VLM comparisons, and an encoder control, strengthening evidence for both central contributions. The human study's inconsistent 5-point versus 0–5 scale description and stronger interpretation of unchanged transfer results remain concerns, but the added validation and comparisons provide a substantial net improvement.
